newsitem.title: UK: GWR plans UK disposal programme.
newsitem.headline: GWR plans UK disposal programme.

text.p: Radio operator GWR Group Plc said on Monday it planned a series of disposals to keep itself within UK ownership limits following its acquisition of Classic FM.
But it said it would not now sell the Leicester Sound station after the Radio Authority blocked a planned disposal to DMG Radio, a Daily Mail and General Trust Plc unit.
The Authority said the result would be too great a concentration of media ownership in the Leicester area, where the Daily Mail group already owns the local newspaper.

As part of the deal, GWR also planned to sell an 11 percent stake in London News Radio Limited to DMG. It said it would have talks with the company to determine whether this disposal, which would cut its stake to 20 percent, could now proceed.

A Daily Mail spokesman said the company had not ruled out buying the London News Radio stake but that the situation was "back to square one" following the collapse of the combined deal with Leicester Sound.
GWR also announced the sale of three AM licences to subsidiaries of unquoted Radio First Plc for 730,000 stg in cash including goodwill.

The three licences are Classic Gold 774 in Cheltenham and Gloucester, Northampton's Classic Gold 1557 and Classic Gold 1332 in Peterborough. GWR will retain the FM licences which broadcast to these areas.
The deal is expected to be completed on Tuesday (January 21) when 225,000 will be paid to Radio First, with the balance to be paid in December 1998.

Acquisitive local radio group GWR bought national commerical station Classic FM for 71.5 million stg in a deal completed last month. Classic, which supplies a diet of light classical music, has a 3.3 percent market share.
